extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting preprints to PCI Ecology
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for authors who wish to submit ecology-related preprints to PCI Ecology, covering scope, mandatory reproducibility/data requirements, ethics, manuscript structure, formatting, submission workflow, and review transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: High scientific, methodological, and ethical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Ecology recommends only preprints that meet high scientific, methodological, and ethical standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommenders select work that stands out for its context, questions, methods, or findings; published recommendations highlight strengths and reasons the recommender found the work interesting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint requirement and exclusivity at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should first post their article on a preprint server or open-access repository. The preprint must not be published or under consideration for evaluation elsewhere at the time of its submission to PCI Ecology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To submit, post on a preprint server (e.g., bioRxiv, arXiv) and then use PCI's 'Submit preprint' flow. PCI Ecology is not obliged to consider every submission; only preprints that attract the interest of a recommender enter review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raw data availability (mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles recommended by PCI must provide raw data (except for ethical reasons) directly in the text or through an open repository with a DOI; data must be reusable with appropriate metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repository examples: Zenodo, Dryad, institutional repositories; data should be described with metadata and accompanying text so others can reuse it. See PCI data-sharing policy for ethical exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis scripts, code, and simulation details (mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Details on quantitative analyses and details concerning simulations (scripts, codes) must be provided in the text or through a correctly versioned deposit in an open repository with a DOI or other permanent identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scripts/codes must be carefully described such that another researcher can run them; Git URLs are not permanent — provide DOI or SWHID; info on issuing a DOI for GitHub is linked in guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear justification of sample sizes (mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical studies must provide a clear justification of sample sizes, with regard to statistical power, Bayes factor thresholds, estimate precision, or for qualitative studies, information power or saturation thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference given: Lakens, 2022; justify sample sizes quantitatively or with appropriate qualitative rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Details on experimental procedures (mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Details on experimental procedures must be given in the text to permit understanding and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials and methods should be sufficiently detailed to allow replication by other researchers; specimen-based studies should provide complete repository information and deposit specimens in accessible permanent repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three mandatory reproducibility rules summary
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI has set three mandatory rules (data, analysis details/scripts, sample-size justification) that articles must follow to promote reproducibility and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mandatory rules are complemented by two suggestions (preregistration and replications). Failure to comply with mandatory rules prevents recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of preregistration and replications
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI encourages preregistrations and welcomes replication studies; preregistrations should be submitted to PCI Registered Reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preregistration clarifies hypotheses and analysis plans, reduces postdiction; all submissions assessed equally if considered interesting by a recommender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical standards and COPE adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer Community In subscribes to COPE principles; financial conflicts of interest are forbidden and non-financial conflicts must be declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See PCI code of conduct for details; authors must declare potential non-financial conflicts and comply with COPE-aligned ethical behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria (ICMJE)
rubrics_metrics.description: All people listed as authors must meet authorship criteria: substantial contribution to study planning/data/interpretation, wrote or critically revised the manuscript, approved the final version, and agree to be accountable for all aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All authors must be aware and agree to be listed; no person meeting criteria should be omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human and animal ethics approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Human-participant studies should meet Declaration of Helsinki principles; animal studies should meet consensus author guidelines on animal ethics and welfare and be approved by an ethical review committee where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should include a statement that informed consent was obtained for human subjects and ensure necessary approvals have been obtained before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity of data and images
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the data presented should be fabricated or distorted, no valid data excluded, and images must not be manipulated to mislead readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must interpret results objectively and alert PCI Ecology if they discover serious errors before or after recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgements, funding, and permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: All sources of funding must be listed; contributors who are not authors must be acknowledged with their consent; permissions must be obtained for unpublished data and copyrighted figures/tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledged contributors are not responsible for the final version; consent must be obtained from owners of previously published figures/tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: No financial conflict of interest (explicit rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial conflicts of interest are forbidden for submissions to PCI Ecology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should declare any potential non-financial conflicts in the Conflict of Interest disclosure section; recommended sentence provided for absence of competing interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI usage: allowed uses and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of AI for translation, correction, or improving text or software code is acceptable if authors review and approve outputs; data analysis with AI is acceptable if methods are published or detailed. Generating text, illustrations and code with AI can be problematic and must be carefully checked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must disclose how they used AI in methods or acknowledgements. Authors must not generate illustrations using AI. Authors must check for plagiarism, hallucinations, and errors. Non-compliance can result in rejection. AI cannot be listed as an author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript deposition and availability at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: At submission, raw data, scripts, codes, and supplementary information must be made available to reviewers and recommenders; after recommendation they must be available to readers in the text or via a correctly versioned deposit with a DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note Git URLs are not permanent; provide DOIs or SWHIDs; data/scripts must be described so another researcher can reuse them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting recommendations (no strict word limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Ecology imposes no strict word limits or formatting but requests guidelines to facilitate peer review: number lines, place tables/figures in main text, define abbreviations, and ensure typographical accuracy because PCI does not copy-edit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PCI Word/LaTeX templates; manuscript should be cohesive and logically organized; be as concise as possible but as long as necessary for clear reproducible rationale and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript structure and section expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical sections include Title, Authors (with affiliations and ORCID), Abstract, Introduction, Materials and Methods, Results, Discussion, Tables/Figures, Acknowledgements, Funding, Conflict of Interest disclosure, Data/scripts/code availability, and References.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title should be unambiguous and understandable to specialists in other fields; abstract concise and present main findings (structured abstracts allowed); introduction must explain reasons and present research question/hypothesis; methods must enable replication; results must have data available and clearly distinguish authors' ideas from others; discussion should answer research questions, compare with published data, state limitations, and ensure conclusions are supported by data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and figures presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables and figures must be located in the main text and be easily understandable without reference to the main body; captions must be informative but concise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All abbreviations used in captions should be defined; ensure figures/tables and supplementary materials are present and accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: References and citation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are free to use their preferred reference style but APA 7 is suggested; provide DOI for references if available; include all references cited in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference list can be alphabetical (author-year) or by order of appearance (numerical). PCI encourages citing original research as primary sources per DORA guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data/scripts/code availability section requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: After recommendation, data, scripts, command lines, and simulation code must be available to readers either in the text or via correctly versioned deposit (DOI or permanent identifier); if not accessible, the reason must be given in the availability section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer machine-readable formats; avoid PDFs for data; README files are required; if DOIs or URLs are provided, cite them in-text and list in references.

rubrics_metrics.name: SORTEE six-stage reproducibility checklist (data & code curation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are expected to fulfill these six criteria for recommendation: (1) data accessible/interoperable/with metadata/licenses; (2) data described by manuscript; (3) code accessible/interoperable/with metadata/licenses; (4) code matches methods; (5) code runs without error; (6) running code with provided data reproduces results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These follow the SORTEE guidelines; PCI data editors may conduct checks in parallel to evaluation. Steps 5 and 6, when conducted, are required to succeed for recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data editor checks and author responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Since March 2025, PCI Ecology may put authors in touch with volunteer data editors who check that deposited data and scripts are findable, reusable, and computationally reproducible; authors are expected to address data editors' concerns promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks are carried out in parallel to evaluation and can start in the first round; authors should prepare data/scripts in advance using the provided checklist and self-assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-assessment questionnaire for manuscript quality (title, abstract, intro, methods, results, discussion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors and reviewers are encouraged to answer specific questions about title/abstract clarity, whether introduction presents research questions and builds on relevant research, methods detail for replication, appropriateness of analyses and sample size justification, correct description/interpretation of results, and whether conclusions are supported and limitations discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This questionnaire helps recommenders make informed decisions; negative responses require prompt rectification before or during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-assessment questionnaire for data/scripts/code
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist questions: can data/scripts be accessed? Are they licensed appropriately? Are formats interoperable? Is there a README? Are README and data comprehensible to a naive reader? Are scripts annotated? Do data and scripts match analyses presented? Do scripts run easily? Do generated outputs match manuscript?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are recommended to send scripts/data to colleagues to test reproducibility; a linked exact checklist and guidance (TADA!, SORTEE) are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common reproducibility pitfalls (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent errors hindering computational reproducibility include absence of script verification, scripts referencing mismatched filenames, use of absolute paths, scripts in languages other than English, inadequate README or script annotations, missing installation instructions, omission of comments on long runtimes, and non-preconfigured package installations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid absolute paths; include installation instructions, sufficiently annotated scripts, and clear README describing purpose and runtime expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender handling: at least two high-quality reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: A recommender who initiates evaluation will invite reviewers to obtain at least two high-quality reviews; recommenders and reviewers must declare no conflicts of interest with content/authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommender signs decisions; reviewers may remain anonymous or sign reviews. Median time to first decision reported as 45 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent review publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Ecology publishes all reviews of recommended manuscripts (reviewers choose whether to sign) and publishes all editorial correspondence (reviews, recommender decisions, authors' replies) for recommended articles. Reviews of rejected submissions are sent to authors but not published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews and recommenders' decision letters are published at the point of acceptance; reviewers and recommenders must adhere to the PCI code of conduct and avoid abusive/discriminatory language; problematic reviews may be edited, returned, or discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous (double-blind) submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can submit anonymously by not depositing on public preprint servers but using a private web interface to provide preprint and data/script links; tick anonymous box and do not include names in cover letter. Names are provided to Managing Board but not to suggested recommenders or reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommenders decide to handle the submission they are provided with authors' names to check conflicts; if recommended, authors must deposit a final non-anonymized version in an open archive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting recommenders at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: During submission, authors are asked to suggest between 5 and 10 recommenders who could handle evaluation; recommenders act similarly to associate editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI Ecology is under no obligation to consider the preprint; only recommenders drive initiation of the evaluation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals process
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of rejected manuscripts can appeal within 30 days by contacting PCI Ecology; appeals considered by the specialist recommender(s) and the Managing Board; decisions following appeal are final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals email provided: contact@ecology.peercommunityin.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation outcome and citation status
rubrics_metrics.description: If recommended, PCI Ecology publishes a short recommendation article signed by the recommender and publishes all editorial correspondence; the preprint remains on the preprint server and becomes a valid citable reference without needing traditional journal publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors remain free to submit recommended preprints to traditional journals; PCI-friendly journals and the Peer Community Journal may accept recommended preprints with no further peer review or fast response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of acceptable submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Ecology recommends preprints addressing questions in ecology about all types of organisms and covers all biology fields provided context and key question relate to ecology; empirical, theoretical, modelling, methodology studies, perspectives, reviews, opinions, and comments are welcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preregistrations should go to PCI Registered Reports; scope includes replication and negative-result studies if interesting to the recommender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript quality expectation (finished article)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recommended article should be as close to perfect as possible in form because PCI Ecology does not copy-edit articles; authors should ensure typographical accuracy and completeness of materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check presence of all tables/figures, additional materials, accessibility of data/scripts/codes, and accuracy of references before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomenclatural acts advisory
rubrics_metrics.description: New biological names and nomenclatural acts in preprints are not considered available under ICN/ICZN because preprints lack ISSN/ISBN and immutability; thus such names should be edited out before submission or published later in a traditional journal to become available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: remove new names from preprints to avoid ambiguity; for availability publish in a journal (e.g., Peer Community Journal) after PCI evaluation.
